claims.claim: 100 million to 1 billion humanoid robots within five years (by ~2031).
claims.source: Public video remarks, 2026 (event/date to verify before publishing)

branches.name: Right but late
branches.desc: Humanoids reach >=1M/yr run rate by 2031; 100M lands 2040s

branches.name: Niche plateau
branches.desc: Robots stay specialized/industrial; no general-purpose breakout this decade

signposts.watch: Any humanoid maker (Optimus, Figure, 1X, Unitree) crossing sustained ~10k units/year production run rate
Disclosed humanoid unit cost under ~$30k at volume
One non-automotive customer deploying 1,000+ humanoids in real operations
Chinese maker pricing below $10k at scale

claims.kill: Under ~1M cumulative units industry-wide by end-2027 kills branch A arithmetically.

claims.claim: Not another platform shift: the end of the computing cycle; a new one built on robotics, edge AI, distributed manufacturing. Starts within 18 months (by early 2028).

branches.name: Software persists
branches.desc: AI-native software keeps compounding as the value engine; no cycle end

signposts.watch: Robotics + edge-AI share of early-stage VC funding hitting record levels
Software incumbent gross margins visibly compressing attributed to AI commoditization
Trajectory of AI-native software leaders (e.g. Lovable): continued hypergrowth supports C; stall supports A/B

claims.kill: AI-native software still producing the era's biggest value creation through 2028 while atoms stay a promise.

claims.claim: The next trillion-dollar European company will be a computing hardware company.

branches.name: European hardware giant forms
branches.desc: A European semis/photonics company on trillion-dollar trajectory within 15 years

branches.name: Ecosystem forms, giant elsewhere
branches.desc: European semis ecosystem strengthens but biggest outcomes exit early or relocate

branches.name: Gap persists
branches.desc: Growth-stage wall holds; talent and IP keep leaking to US/Asia

signposts.watch: Specialized European growth capital (A/B rounds) for semiconductors emerging - new funds or repeated European-led B rounds
Chips Act pilot lines operational and used by startups (Espoo, Tampere, IMEC, Fraunhofer, Grenoble)
European hardware IP exits at substantial pre-revenue valuations continuing
Cloudberry's promised sharper theses at six-month follow-up (Feb 2027)

claims.kill: Through 2028, Europe's best semiconductor companies still relocate or sell early to US/Asia for lack of domestic capital.

claims.claim: AI infrastructure buildout (energy, datacenters, chips, HBM) overshoots demand due to long lead times; a dark-fiber-style bust follows, even though the infrastructure is useful long-term.

branches.name: Bullwhip bust
branches.desc: Supply overshoots; capex crash within 3-4 years; assets later productive (dark fiber pattern)

branches.name: Soft landing
branches.desc: Demand grows into supply; margins compress but no crash

branches.name: Persistent shortage
branches.desc: Demand keeps outrunning supply through the decade

signposts.watch: Datacenter vacancy rates / delayed or cancelled DC projects appearing
HBM/advanced packaging moving from allocation (shortage) to inventory (glut)
Power purchase prices for DC campuses: falling spot deals signal oversupply

claims.kill: GPU/DC utilization stays saturated with waitlists through 2029.
